quizExplanations.d1: The Kaaba is the holy site Muslims face while praying.
quizExplanations.d2: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from dawn until sunset.
quizExplanations.d3: Saying "Bismillah" means starting something in the name of Allah.
quizExplanations.d4: A mosque is a holy place where Muslims pray and worship.
quizExplanations.d5: The Eid al-Fitr festival is celebrated after the month of fasting ends.
quizExplanations.d6: The Quran has a chapter called "An-Nahl", which means "The Bee".
quizExplanations.e11: Treating parents with respect and kindness is very important in Islam.
quizExplanations.e12: Honesty is a beautiful trait, while lying is wrong.
quizExplanations.e13: Helping others makes us better people.
quizExplanations.e14: Caring for orphans is a highly rewarded good deed.
quizExplanations.e15: Cleanliness matters for both health and good character.
quizExplanations.sc13: A rainbow has 7 colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
quizExplanations.sc14: The Moon is the natural satellite that orbits the Earth.
quizExplanations.sc15: The lion is called the "king of the forest" because of its strength.
quizExplanations.sc16: Bees make honey from the nectar they collect from flowers.
quizExplanations.sc17: Penguins can't fly, but they swim very fast in water.
quizExplanations.sc18: Throwing trash in the right place helps protect nature.
quizExplanations.d7: Muslims everywhere in the world face the Kaaba in Makkah when they pray. This direction is called the qibla.
quizExplanations.d8: The Quran begins with Surah Al-Fatiha. This surah is also recited in every prayer.
quizExplanations.d9: 'Bismillah' means 'in the name of Allah.' It is said before eating to give thanks to Allah for the food.
quizExplanations.d10: 'Inshallah' means 'if Allah wills.' It is said when talking about future plans, because everything happens by Allah's will.
quizExplanations.d11: During Eid al-Adha, Muslims sacrifice an animal as a sign of obedience to Allah and share the meat with those in need.
quizExplanations.d12: Iftar is when the fast is broken at sunset and eating begins. It is one of the beautiful moments of Ramadan.
quizExplanations.d13: Sadaqah is help given freely from the heart, without any obligation. Even a small act of kindness counts as sadaqah.
quizExplanations.e16: Being kind to animals is one of the beautiful teachings our Prophet showed us.
quizExplanations.e17: Helping and respecting elderly people is a very rewarding good deed.
quizExplanations.e18: Helping younger children and being kind to them is a wonderful quality.
quizExplanations.e19: Thanking someone who does good to us is part of good manners.
quizExplanations.e20: Supporting a sad friend and being there for them is a beautiful deed.
quizExplanations.sc19: A day has 24 hours — the time it takes Earth to complete one full spin on its axis.
quizExplanations.sc20: A giraffe's long neck helps it reach the high leaves on trees.
quizExplanations.sc21: The elephant is the largest land animal and uses its trunk to drink water and grab food.
quizExplanations.sc22: Every zebra's stripes are different, just like a human fingerprint.
quizExplanations.sc23: Pandas eat bamboo for many hours a day — it is their main food.
quizExplanations.sc24: A kangaroo raises its baby in the pouch on its belly after it is born.
quizExplanations.sc25: A camel stores fat in its hump, which helps it survive without water for a long time in the desert.
quizExplanations.sc26: An owl's eyes are made for seeing in the dark, which is why it hunts at night.
quizExplanations.sc27: Dolphins are very intelligent animals and "talk" to each other using sounds.
quizExplanations.sc28: We live on the planet called Earth in our solar system.
quizExplanations.sc29: When water cools below 0 degrees, it freezes and turns into ice.
quizExplanations.m21: This is the odd-number sequence: it increases by 2 each time — 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.
quizExplanations.m22: 9 - 4 = 5. There are 5 birds left on the tree.
quizExplanations.d14: Prophet Adam (peace be upon him) was the first human Allah created and the first prophet.
quizExplanations.d15: Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) built a ship by Allah's command to be saved from the great flood.
quizExplanations.d16: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was known for his strong faith in Allah and his trust in Him through every hardship.
quizExplanations.d17: Prophet Ismail (peace be upon him) is the son of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and was himself a prophet.
quizExplanations.d18: Our Prophet (peace be upon him) was always kind, gentle, and caring toward children.
quizExplanations.e21: Being genuinely happy for a friend's success is a beautiful quality.
quizExplanations.e22: We should do good deeds to please Allah, without expecting anything in return — that is the most valuable kind of good deed.
quizExplanations.sc30: The Sun always rises in the east — this is a result of the Earth's rotation on its axis.
quizExplanations.sc31: The Sun always sets in the west, because the Earth rotates from west to east.
quizExplanations.sc32: The blue whale is the largest animal on Earth and it lives in the sea.
quizExplanations.sc33: Birds' wings help them fly through the air.
quizExplanations.sc34: Fish breathe by taking in oxygen dissolved in water through their gills.
quizExplanations.sc35: A rainbow is a beautiful color phenomenon caused by sunlight bending through raindrops.
quizExplanations.sc36: A turtle has a hard shell protecting its body, as if it carries its own house on its back.
quizExplanations.sc37: In autumn, trees prepare for winter, and their leaves change color and fall.
quizExplanations.sc38: Water is very important for life, so we must use it carefully and protect it.
quizExplanations.m31: Each number is double the one before it: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.

yunus: Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) was sent by Allah as a messenger to the people of Nineveh. He called them to believe in Allah and follow the right path.
His people did not listen to him for a long time. Yunus (peace be upon him) became upset and left the city without waiting for Allah's permission, boarding a ship.
A powerful storm hit the sea. To make the ship lighter, the sailors drew lots, and the lot fell on Yunus. He was thrown into the sea, and by Allah's command, a huge fish swallowed him.

Inside the fish, in the depths of the dark sea, Yunus (peace be upon him) realized his mistake and called out to Allah with all his heart: "There is no god but You, glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers."
Allah accepted his sincere repentance. The fish released him onto the shore. Yunus (peace be upon him) was very weak, so Allah made a plant grow over him to give him shade and food.

Yunus (peace be upon him) returned to his people. By then, they had already come to believe, and they were saved. This story teaches us: Allah forgives anyone who repents sincerely — even in the darkest moment.
ibrahim: Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) grew up in a society that worshipped idols, but from an early age he believed in the oneness of Allah.
He tried to explain to his father and his people that idols made of stone and wood could neither help nor harm anyone, but they would not listen to him.

One day, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) broke all the idols except the largest one and hung the axe on it. When the people returned and asked him, he said: "The big one did it — ask it, if it can speak."
The people grew angry and decided to burn him in a great fire. But Allah commanded the fire: "O fire, be cool and safe for Ibrahim!" And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) came out unharmed.
Later, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) built the Kaaba in Makkah together with his son Ismail (peace be upon him) — the first house built for people to worship Allah.

Because of his strong trust and faith in Allah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was called "Khalilullah" — the Friend of Allah. This story teaches us: Allah protects everyone who holds firmly to true faith in Him, in every hardship.
musa: Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) was born in Egypt, during the rule of a cruel pharaoh who had ordered that every newborn boy be killed.
By Allah's inspiration, his mother placed baby Musa in a basket and set it on the river. The basket reached Pharaoh's palace, and Musa grew up there, among Pharaoh's own family.
When he grew up, Musa (peace be upon him) had to leave Egypt. Years later, on Mount Sinai, Allah sent him revelation and chose him as a prophet, turning his staff into a miraculous sign.
Allah sent Musa (peace be upon him), together with his brother Harun (peace be upon him), to Pharaoh, to free the Children of Israel and call people to the truth. Pharaoh stubbornly refused.
Musa (peace be upon him) led his people out of Egypt at night. Pharaoh and his army chased after them and caught up with them at the shore of the Red Sea.

By Allah's command, Musa (peace be upon him) struck the sea with his staff, and it split into two. His people crossed safely on dry land, but when Pharaoh and his army followed them in, the sea closed again.
This story teaches us: Allah always shows a way out to those who trust and remain patient in Him, even in the hardest moments.

duaMeaning.morning: O my Lord! With Your help we have reached the morning, and with Your help we reach the evening.
duaMeaning.morning2: Praise be to Allah who gave us life after taking it from us in sleep, and to Him is the return.
duaMeaning.morning3: O my Lord, increase me in knowledge.
duaMeaning.evening: O my Lord! With Your help we have reached the evening, and with Your help we reach the morning.
duaMeaning.evening2: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
duaMeaning.evening3: O my Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor.
duaMeaning.sleep: In Your name, O Allah, I die (sleep) and I live (wake up).
duaMeaning.sleep2: O my Lord, protect me from Your punishment.
duaMeaning.sleep3: In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in Your name I raise it up again.
duaMeaning.eat2: Praise be to Allah who fed us, gave us drink, and made us Muslims.
duaMeaning.eat3: In the name of Allah, at its beginning and at its end.
